analysis.title: Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN): Robust expense discipline and growth in newer products, offset by weaker near-term revenue outlook
key_insights: COIN reported 3Q26 EPS of $2.51 vs GSe +$1.88 and consensus -$0.04. Excluding one-timers, GS pegs core EPS at $0.71 vs GSe $0.54 and consensus $0.48, driven by core operating expenses (ex. SBC) 5% below the Street.
GS expects a modestly negative stock reaction to the print because of the weaker outlook, despite the quarterly beat.

GS argues that in a persistently tepid crypto trading environment COIN offers greater scale, profitability and distribution than competitors, plus ongoing expansion into prediction markets and crypto derivatives.

COIN guided 4Q26 adj. operating expenses down $100mn at the midpoint to $1.007bn-1.157bn and FY26 to $4.15bn-4.3bn. This is the second FY26 opex guide-down this year, a cumulative $200mn (5%) reduction YTD.
Prediction markets passed ~$200mn annualized revenue in 3Q26, up from ~$100mn in 2Q26 and compounding 82% quarterly since 1Q26. DAUs rose >60% QoQ and non-sports contracts were >50% of volumes.

COIN received a Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO) license that lets it list event contracts as a Designated Contract Market (DCM). COIN could then earn both brokerage and exchange fees and control contract design.
3Q26 was the fifth consecutive quarter of record high-value Coinbase One (CB1) paid subscribers. CB1 customers generate 3.5x the ARPU of other COIN users, with higher retention.
Total payment volume on the Coinbase Developer Platform has compounded 160% quarterly since 4Q25, driven by stablecoin payments and infrastructure.
4Q26 quarter-to-date transaction revenue is ~$165mn. Run-rated for the full quarter that is ~$607mn, 11% below consensus after day-count adjustment.
4Q26 subscription and services revenue guidance is $550-630mn, with a midpoint ~5% below consensus.
GS cuts 2026E/27E/28E total revenue by 4%/8%/5% and adj. expenses (ex. SBC) by 2%/3%/1%. Adj. pre-tax margins (ex. SBC) fall by 2.2pp/3.9pp/2.6pp.
GS cuts 2026E/27E/28E adj. EPS by 3%/18%/10%. The target P/E on Q5-Q8 EPS drops 3.0x to 30.0x, and the 12-month price target falls 14% to $210 from $244. Rating stays Buy.

3Q26 transaction revenue was $590mn, in line with consensus and down 44% YoY. Retail was 1% above and institutional 7% below the Street. Management said prediction markets have not cannibalized spot crypto trading volumes.
Non-US tokenized equities trading has seen early robust adoption, with >$3bn of volume since launch.

3Q26 subscription and services revenue was $570mn, -2% vs GSe and +1% vs consensus, and down 24% YoY. Other and staking revenue were 4% and 3% below the Street, while interest and stablecoin revenue were 7% and 3% above.
Prime brokerage expanded, with average daily loan book balance up 74% YoY.
3Q26 adj. expenses (ex. SBC) were $921mn, down 21% YoY and 8% below consensus. G&A and tech and dev were 10% and 4% lower, partly offset by transaction-related expense 9% higher.

FY26E adj. expense guidance of $4.15bn-4.30bn is 1% below the Street at the midpoint, and the 4Q26E midpoint is 4% below implied Street estimates. 4Q26 guidance also includes transaction expenses in the mid-teens as a % of net revenue and SBC of ~$240mn.

market_movers.rationale: GS cut the 12-month PT 14% to $210 from $244 on lower estimates and a lower target multiple of 30.0x Q5-Q8 EPS. Buy rating kept with 30.8% upside to $160.59.

earnings_insights: COIN 3Q26 reported EPS $2.51 vs GSe +$1.88 and Visible Alpha consensus -$0.04. All three are reported or estimate figures including one-timers.

COIN 3Q26 core EPS ex one-timers (adjusted for data theft recovery, restructuring, crypto asset gains/losses incl. a $210mn loss on crypto assets held for investment, normalized tax rate and ex SBC) is $0.71 reported vs GSe $0.54 and consensus $0.48.
3Q26 transaction revenue $590mn reported, in line with consensus, down 44% YoY.
3Q26 subscription and services revenue $570mn reported, -2% vs GSe and +1% vs consensus, down 24% YoY.
3Q26 adj. expenses ex SBC $921mn reported, down 21% YoY, 8% below consensus.

4Q26 company guidance: adj. opex $1.007bn-1.157bn, subscription and services revenue $550-630mn, SBC ~$240mn, transaction expenses mid-teens % of net revenue. QTD 4Q26 transaction revenue is ~$165mn (company update).
FY26 adj. opex guidance lowered to $4.15bn-4.3bn from a prior range ~$100mn higher at the midpoint.

GS estimates: FY26E EPS $2.43 (old $2.50), FY27E $5.02 (old $6.12), FY28E $7.61 (old $8.47). Revenue FY26E $5,179mn (old $5,386mn), FY27E $6,982mn (old $7,565mn), FY28E $8,700mn (old $9,171mn). All are GS forecasts.
GS quarterly EPS forecasts: 4Q26E $0.22, 1Q27E $0.92, 2Q27E $1.20. 3Q26 EPS shown in the table is $3.21 (the report labels the column 9/26 with no further qualifier).
crypto_views: COIN's 3Q26 results are framed against a persistently tepid crypto trading environment.
Prediction markets reached ~$200mn annualized revenue, with non-sports contracts >50% of volumes, largely driven by crypto prediction markets.
Non-US tokenized equities trading has exceeded $3bn of volume since launch.
Coinbase Developer Platform total payment volume has compounded 160% quarterly since 4Q25 on stablecoin payments and infrastructure.
Interest and stablecoin revenue ran 7% (GSe) and 3% (consensus) above estimates, while staking and other revenue ran below.
GS lists the crypto-related downside risks as insufficient deregulatory reform and crypto market cap trending down over time.
risk_factors: Product evolution outside of trading takes longer than expected.
Crypto market cap trends down over time.

tension_points.theme: COIN near-term revenue vs platform growth
tension_points.bull_case: Expense discipline (cumulative $200mn or 5% FY26 opex cut YTD), prediction markets at ~$200mn annualized revenue, record CB1 subscribers, and stablecoin payments growth support a constructive long-term view. GS keeps a Buy and a $210 target.
tension_points.bear_case: 4Q26 quarter-to-date transaction revenue of ~$165mn is 11% below the Street on a day-count adjusted basis, and the subscription and services guide midpoint is ~5% below. GS cut FY26E-28E revenue by 4%/8%/5% and adj. EPS by 3%/18%/10%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS names no specific level, but lists risks to the Buy thesis: insufficient crypto deregulatory reform, slower product evolution outside trading, a falling crypto market cap and pricing pressure on margins.
